question: Should ClickClack permanently support shared, durable channel pins as a public API/SDK and exportable data-model feature, including the stated 100-pin limit and pin lifecycle events?
rationale: This PR establishes new durable schema, public operations, and realtime event names; the implementation can be repaired mechanically, but accepting the lasting product and compatibility contract requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor the public pin contract
options.body: Accept shared channel pins as a supported product feature and require the lifecycle, export, and race fixes before merge.

options.title: Narrow to an internal experiment
options.body: Avoid committing to public SDK/event compatibility by redesigning the feature behind an explicitly non-public boundary before merge.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Pause this PR until a maintainer confirms shared pins are a current product priority.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the public pin contract
recommendation.body: Accept shared channel pins as a supported product feature and require the lifecycle, export, and race fixes before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the proposed cross-layer implementation and can incorporate the mechanical fixes once a maintainer sponsors the contract.
